title: Evaluation of Breathing, Sleep and the Effects of Continuous Positive Airway Pressure During Wakefulness in Children With Heart Failure

sections.abstract: Adult patients with heart failure (HF) have an increased work of breathing and are at increased risk for obstructive and/or central apnea during sleep. Noninvasive continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) has proved its efficacy in decreasing the work of breathing and improving sleep-disordered breathing in these patients. The aim of the study is to analyze the work of breathing and objective and subjective sleep quality in children with HF and to evaluate the ability of noninvasive CPAP to decrease the work of breathing and improve cardiac output during wakefulness.
